messages.subject: Prior defaults and Comparing parameters across groups
messages.subject_clean: Prior defaults and Comparing parameters across groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have two questions.

(1) Is there any literature on why the default priors in blavaan are what they are (I'm trying to get a feel for what the default priors represent with respect to subjective beliefs as a starting point for developing an intuition for what I might change them for in my given research situation).

(2) Is it possible to compare a particular parameter across two groups. To be specific, I'm doing a latent growth model with two predictors of the slope/intercept. In a general form my model is something like this:

---
model1 <- '  i =~ 1*OutcomeT1 + 1* OutcomeT2 + 1* OutcomeT3
s =~ 0* OutcomeT1 + 9* OutcomeT2 + 36* OutcomeT3

#variances/covariances
i ~~ i
s ~~ s
i ~~ s

#intercepts
i ~ 1
s ~ 1
OutcomeT1 ~ 0
OutcomeT2 ~ 0
OutcomeT3 ~ 0

i ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
s ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
'
----

In which my time intervals are 0, 9 months and 36 months (hence the loadings for s). I have two groups (let's call them A and B).

I want to establish whether the regression parameter for predictor2 on the intercept for growth is plausibly the same in groups A and B. Let's say I run model 1 above in group A and the parameter estimate is 0.07. In a classical model, (I think) I'd do something like run a model in group B where I constrain the parameter of interest to be 0.07, the value in group A. Then i'd compare fit indices for group B of model 1 (unconstrained) and model 2 (constrained) to get a p-value. So, something like (change in bold):

---
model2 <- '  i =~ 1*OutcomeT1 + 1* OutcomeT2 + 1* OutcomeT3
s =~ 0* OutcomeT1 + 9* OutcomeT2 + 36* OutcomeT3

#variances/covariances
i ~~ i
s ~~ s
i ~~ s

#intercepts
i ~ 1
s ~ 1
OutcomeT1 ~ 0
OutcomeT2 ~ 0
OutcomeT3 ~ 0

i ~ Predictor1 + 0.07*Predictor2
s ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
'

fit.model1.gpB<- growth(model1, data=df)
fit.model2.gpB<- growth(model2, data=df)

anova(fit.model1.gpB, fit.model2.gpB)
---

I have successfully fit these models using blavaan with default priors (and even changed priors, although I don't have a strong intuition at present about what my changes represent with respect to subjective beliefs). My question is whether I can get a Bayesian equivalent of the above comparison. So, rather than look at a p-value that compares models with and without the parameter of interest constrained, get something like a HPD for the difference in the value of the parameter estimate in group A and B. Ideally I'd like a posterior distribution where I can look at whether the probability mass is around 0 (which I think would tell me that evidence strongly favours the parameters being the same) or whether it is shifted away from zero sufficiently for me to believe that the parameter estimates are plausibly different in groups A and B.

I am very new to both latent growth models and Bayesian stats, so please excuse any idiocy in the question!

Thanks in advance for any help/pointers.

andy

messages.subject: Re: Prior defaults and Comparing parameters across groups
messages.subject_clean: Prior defaults and Comparing parameters across groups
messages.body_plain:
Andy,

The default priors in blavaan were designed to be relatively flat/uninformative, in the sense that they return estimates similar to ML estimates for many models. In JAGS (the engine that does model estimation), it seems that very flat priors (flatter than those in blavaan) can harm convergence. So the blavaan priors also try to balance this issue. I could be convinced that other defaults are better.

Regarding setting your own priors, it seems like the key is to focus on how each of your model parameters could be interpreted. Literature on frequentist models would be as helpful here as literature on Bayesian models. Then, based on the parameter interpretation, it is often easier to decide parameter values that are plausible/implausible and to set priors.

Regarding comparing a parameter value across two groups, I see two main options. Both make use of the "group" argument, which allows you to fit a two-group model in one go. This argument can also be used in blavaan, so that you are not fitting the same model twice.

1. Fit two models, (i) a two-group model where the focal parameter is constrained equal across groups and (ii) a two-group model where the focal parameter is free for each group. Compare these models via their fitMeasures().

2. Fit a single model where the focal parameter is named in each group. Then define a new variable that is the difference between parameters. The model syntax might be modified to be something like:

i ~ Predictor1 + c("g1int", "g2int")*Predictor2

pardiff := g1int - g2int

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Ed, thats very helpful.

Method 1 that you suggest works just fine, but method 2 is more what I'm after. I actually set up 4 user-defined variables that are differences in key parameters in groups A and B. (My earlier use of 1 parameter was to keep the example simple).  In lavaan method 2 works great, but when I run using blavaan I get an error:

Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "est", value = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 9, 36,  :
  replacement has 55 rows, data has 59

I'm guessing this is because my 4 user-defined parameters are making the 'data' longer than what jags/blavaan is expecting based on the rest of the model specification. Put another way, it's not recognizing my user defined parameters. Have I interpreted the error correctly and is there a way around this?

If all else fails I have plotted the HPDs for the parameters of interest in the two groups, which to me (but perhaps not reviewers) shows fairly clearly the 'evidence' for whether they are plausibly the same or not, and I can compare fit indices using your method 1, it'd just be nice to have a HPD for the group differences in parameters if it's possible.

Thanks - and no worries if you don't have time to respond.

best wishes
andy

> > > > > On Wednesday, 5 October 2016 20:39:25 UTC+1, Ed Merkle wrote:
> > > > > > Andy,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > The default priors in blavaan were designed to be relatively flat/uninformative, in the sense that they return estimates similar to ML estimates for many models. In JAGS (the engine that does model estimation), it seems that very flat priors (flatter than those in blavaan) can harm convergence. So the blavaan priors also try to balance this issue. I could be convinced that other defaults are better.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Regarding setting your own priors, it seems like the key is to focus on how each of your model parameters could be interpreted. Literature on frequentist models would be as helpful here as literature on Bayesian models. Then, based on the parameter interpretation, it is often easier to decide parameter values that are plausible/implausible and to set priors.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Regarding comparing a parameter value across two groups, I see two main options. Both make use of the "group" argument, which allows you to fit a two-group model in one go. This argument can also be used in blavaan, so that you are not fitting the same model twice.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 1. Fit two models, (i) a two-group model where the focal parameter is constrained equal across groups and (ii) a two-group model where the focal parameter is free for each group. Compare these models via their fitMeasures().
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 2. Fit a single model where the focal parameter is named in each group. Then define a new variable that is the difference between parameters. The model syntax might be modified to be something like:
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > i ~ Predictor1 + c("g1int", "g2int")*Predictor2
> > > > > >
> > > > > > pardiff := g1int - g2int
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Ed
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Wednesday, October 5, 2016 at 9:07:46 AM UTC-5, Andy Field wrote:
> > > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I have two questions.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > (1) Is there any literature on why the default priors in blavaan are what they are (I'm trying to get a feel for what the default priors represent with respect to subjective beliefs as a starting point for developing an intuition for what I might change them for in my given research situation).
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > (2) Is it possible to compare a particular parameter across two groups. To be specific, I'm doing a latent growth model with two predictors of the slope/intercept. In a general form my model is something like this:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > ---
> > > > > > > model1 <- '  i =~ 1*OutcomeT1 + 1* OutcomeT2 + 1* OutcomeT3
> > > > > > > s =~ 0* OutcomeT1 + 9* OutcomeT2 + 36* OutcomeT3
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > #variances/covariances
> > > > > > > i ~~ i
> > > > > > > s ~~ s
> > > > > > > i ~~ s
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > #intercepts
> > > > > > > i ~ 1
> > > > > > > s ~ 1
> > > > > > > OutcomeT1 ~ 0
> > > > > > > OutcomeT2 ~ 0
> > > > > > > OutcomeT3 ~ 0
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > i ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
> > > > > > > s ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
> > > > > > > '
> > > > > > > ----
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > In which my time intervals are 0, 9 months and 36 months (hence the loadings for s). I have two groups (let's call them A and B).
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I want to establish whether the regression parameter for predictor2 on the intercept for growth is plausibly the same in groups A and B. Let's say I run model 1 above in group A and the parameter estimate is 0.07. In a classical model, (I think) I'd do something like run a model in group B where I constrain the parameter of interest to be 0.07, the value in group A. Then i'd compare fit indices for group B of model 1 (unconstrained) and model 2 (constrained) to get a p-value. So, something like (change in bold):
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > ---
> > > > > > > model2 <- '  i =~ 1*OutcomeT1 + 1* OutcomeT2 + 1* OutcomeT3
> > > > > > > s =~ 0* OutcomeT1 + 9* OutcomeT2 + 36* OutcomeT3
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > #variances/covariances
> > > > > > > i ~~ i
> > > > > > > s ~~ s
> > > > > > > i ~~ s
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > #intercepts
> > > > > > > i ~ 1
> > > > > > > s ~ 1
> > > > > > > OutcomeT1 ~ 0
> > > > > > > OutcomeT2 ~ 0
> > > > > > > OutcomeT3 ~ 0
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > i ~ Predictor1 + 0.07*Predictor2
> > > > > > > s ~ Predictor1 + Predictor2
> > > > > > > '
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > fit.model1.gpB<- growth(model1, data=df)
> > > > > > > fit.model2.gpB<- growth(model2, data=df)
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > anova(fit.model1.gpB, fit.model2.gpB)
> > > > > > > ---
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I have successfully fit these models using blavaan with default priors (and even changed priors, although I don't have a strong intuition at present about what my changes represent with respect to subjective beliefs). My question is whether I can get a Bayesian equivalent of the above comparison. So, rather than look at a p-value that compares models with and without the parameter of interest constrained, get something like a HPD for the difference in the value of the parameter estimate in group A and B. Ideally I'd like a posterior distribution where I can look at whether the probability mass is around 0 (which I think would tell me that evidence strongly favours the parameters being the same) or whether it is shifted away from zero sufficiently for me to believe that the parameter estimates are plausibly different in groups A and B.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I am very new to both latent growth models and Bayesian stats, so please excuse any idiocy in the question!
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Thanks in advance for any help/pointers.
